stem: In a stable school-aged child undergoing lumbar puncture, which needle technique is most appropriate once the needle has been inserted?

options.text: Aim the needle towards the umbilicus and advance slowly
Aim the needle towards the coccyx and advance briskly
Advance the needle perpendicular to the skin without using landmarks
Aim the needle laterally towards the flank
Redirect the needle cephalad towards the sternum

explanation: Aim the needle towards the umbilicus and advance slowly. This is because this is the standard lumbar puncture trajectory described for safe needle advancement once the interspace has been identified.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the needle should be directed towards the umbilicus and advanced slowly during lumbar puncture.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the needle is not directed towards the coccyx, and brisk advancement is not the recommended technique.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because lumbar puncture requires a deliberate trajectory guided by body landmarks, not blind perpendicular advancement.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the needle should stay in the midline and be directed towards the umbilicus, not laterally.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because cephalad redirection towards the sternum is not the recommended lumbar puncture trajectory.
